With our conference coming a week following a historic US presidential election that helped boost bank stocks by 12%, bank management teams were generally optimistic with regards to the economic outlook heading into 2017. Greater fiscal stimulus that is expected to spur economic growth coupled with potential regulatory relief has helped
improve the overall sentiment in the sector. When asked what the biggest impact of the GOP sweep would likely be to bank earnings, 35% noted tax cuts and infrastructure spurring growth as the biggest impact.

An area that has attracted particular attention among bank investors is around the current landscape of multifamily lending. We polled the audience around their outlook for multifamily lending in 2017 and found that 49% of those polled said there was some concern, but only in certain regions and at certain rental price points. Meanwhile, 29%
noted softening fundamentals that should lead to slower financing activity and worsening credit metrics (see Chart 4).
